arrangements.title: Promises Kept
arrangements.label: Contemporary Christian
sheet: Before the world had learned to wake,
God spoke a name across the dark —
A promise running like a river
Through every broken and believing heart.
From Adam's altar to Isaiah,
From Simeon's long years at the temple door,
They all kept something they could barely carry
And passed it to the ones who came before.
And maybe you know something of that waiting —
The years that no one sees but you and Him.
He came for the hidden years.
He came for the ordinary days.
He lived the weight of what you're carrying —
Tired hands and grief and unpraised faithfulness.
He came. He came.
Not to the ready and the great —
To Mary's arms and Joseph's hands
And every heart that dared to wait.
Mary said yes before she understood.
Joseph carried shame to shield the one he loved.
A refuge, a child in Egypt, brown-skinned and dependent —
God learned what it is to need.
For eighteen years, the record holds its silence —
Stone and wood and prayer from dawn until night.
The parables He told were not invented;
They were things He'd seen with His own eyes.
So when He says, "I know your sorrows,"
He knows them from the inside, not above.
He came for the hidden years.
He came for the ordinary days.
He lived the weight of what you're carrying —
Tired hands and grief and unpraised faithfulness.
He came. He came.
Not to the ready and the great —
To Mary's arms and Joseph's hands
And every heart that dared to wait.
Your hidden years are not a gap,
The ground for what is building yet.
The preparation was the point —
He never once forgot.
What promise have you been carrying
Through the seasons no one sees?
He named the answer long before you asked,
And He is faithful. He is faithful.
He came for the hidden years.
He came for the ordinary days.
He came for you and all your unseen seasons,
And every hidden year. He understands.
He came. He came.
And He is coming still
To every heart that dares to wait.
He always will.
Wait on the Lord.
He knows your name.
He kept His word.
